questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fixed cost?
options: Water and electricity based on usage

questions.question: If you sell zero items this month, what happens to your fixed costs?
What happens to total variable costs when you sell more items?

subtopics.title: Making a Profit on One Item (Contribution Margin)

questions.question: How do you calculate the contribution margin per unit?
options: Selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit
Selling price per unit plus variable cost per unit
Total fixed costs minus variable cost per unit
Variable cost per unit divided by selling price per unit

questions.question: If a unit sells for R100 and its variable cost is R40, what is the contribution margin?
Why is the contribution margin not your pure profit?
options: Because you still need to pay fixed costs
Because the government takes it as tax
Because the selling price might change

questions.question: What is the break-even point?
options: The point where total revenue equals total costs (no profit, no loss)
The point where you make the maximum profit
The point where fixed costs are zero
The point where you must close the business

questions.question: If fixed costs are R10 000 and contribution margin per unit is R100, what is the break-even point?
If you sell fewer units than the break-even point, you are making a...
What is the correct formula for the break-even point in units?
options: Total Fixed Costs / (Selling Price per unit - Variable Cost per unit)
(Selling Price per unit - Variable Cost per unit) / Total Fixed Costs
Total Fixed Costs / Variable Cost per unit
Total Fixed Costs * (Selling Price per unit - Variable Cost per unit)

questions.question: In the exam, why is it important to show the full formula and substitution?
options: Because marks are awarded for the process and format, not just the final answer
Because the final answer is always wrong
Because the examiner doesn't know the answer

questions.question: If fixed costs are R45 000, selling price is R60, and variable cost is R45, what is the break-even point?
Why is physical stock counting important for break-even?
options: If stock is stolen, you still pay the variable cost but lose the selling price, forcing you to sell more to break even
It decreases the amount of tax you pay

questions.question: What is an internal control?
options: A system or process put in place to prevent errors and theft
The rent paid to the landlord

questions.question: If 100 units are stolen, what happens to the break-even point calculation?
options: The calculation itself doesn't change, but in reality, you must sell 100 *more* units just to cover the cost of the stolen ones
